string-escape.comment: Backslash escapes inside a quoted string (e.g. the \n seen throughout the real corpus's PRINT LIST='...\n' values) -- constant.character.escape, the same scope Python/JS/shell grammars all use for this, so it reads distinctly from the surrounding string text under any theme.
string-escape.name: constant.character.escape.drut

variable-ref.comment: @name@ substitution. Split into begin/name/end captures using the widely-theme-supported punctuation.definition.variable + variable.other.readwrite scopes (the same convention shell-script grammars use for $VAR) rather than a single custom leaf scope -- a bare variable.other.substitution.<lang> scope (this grammar's own original choice) doesn't match most themes' color rules at all, since theme selectors are scope-chain prefixes and few themes have a rule for the literal segment "substitution" (found via real manual VS Code testing, 2026-08-10: @MODE@ rendered with no color whatsoever under a stock dark theme).

statement-words.comment: General (non-block-structural) statement/procedure words -- deliberately a *different* scope (support.function, the conventional TextMate category for a language's built-in commands/procedures, as distinct from true control-flow keywords) so they read visually distinct from control-words above, the same two-tier convention most language grammars use for control-flow vs. builtin-function keywords. Real-usage-evidenced (constitution Principle II: never vendor-doc-copied) -- corpus census against the full 161-file WF-TDM-Official-Releases corpus, 2026-08-10, same distinct_files>=3 threshold 001-voyager-script-parser/003-lsp-vscode-extension's own censuses already established, words already covered by control-words above excluded. Not exhaustive by construction (any word not in this list still parses and functions identically -- FR-003 establishes there's no closed vocabulary -- it just renders unstyled, the same as before this list existed).
statement-words.name: support.function.drut

pair-keywords.comment: A keyword=value pair's keyword name (optionally bracket-subscripted, e.g. VOL[01]=), colored like a Python keyword argument's parameter name (func(param=value)) -- variable.parameter, distinct from control-words/statement-words above. Deliberately structural/generic (matches FR-003's `word[subscript]=` shape from voyager-core's own grammar, not a fixed name list) rather than vendor-sourced, since FR-003 already establishes there's no closed keyword vocabulary. Listed after control-words/statement-words in the top-level patterns array so a word like PHASE (control-words) or PRINT (statement-words) that's *also* immediately followed by = still gets its more specific scope -- TextMate resolves same-position ties by array order.

pair-values.comment: A bareword value immediately after = (or <=/>=/<>/==, since the lookbehind only checks for a literal = as the last character of whatever operator preceded it) -- e.g. MATRIX/HWYASSIGN in PGM=MATRIX/PGM=HWYASSIGN, real Cube Voyager program names with no closed enumeration this grammar hand-lists (same FR-003 no-closed-vocabulary stance as #pair-keywords/#statement-words) -- colored generically as constant.other, the same convention many grammars use for an enum-like bareword value distinct from a quoted string or a number. Deliberately does not fire inside a quoted string (this pattern is top-level-only; #strings' own begin/end block has its own separate, short patterns list -- variable-ref and string-escape only -- so string *content* is never reachable from here).
pair-values.name: constant.other.drut

numbers.comment: A numeric literal, negative sign included only when it can't plausibly be a binary minus (guarded by the same not-preceded-by-alnum-or-closing-bracket lookbehind an operator-precedence-aware tokenizer would use) -- e.g. ZONES=-5's -5 is one number, but 2-2's - is left for #operators to claim as subtraction.
numbers.name: constant.numeric.drut

operators.comment: Symbol-only, structural -- no word-shaped logical operators (AND/OR/NOT-style) included, since those would need the same real-corpus evidence standard this grammar already holds keyword lists to, and none has been gathered for them.
operators.name: keyword.operator.drut
